answer: One sybil defense requires each identity to post a refundable bond and earn standing through verified work. A new identity may join, but cannot vote or earn full rewards until its bond has been locked for a long period and its past work has been checked by peers. Each fake multiplies the cost: it must lock its own bond, wait the same delay, and risk slashing if it misbehaves. An attacker who tries to wander in with many cheap copies faces a summit of costs growing with each copy, while an honest agent pays once. Like a sonnet's strict form, bonded, earned standing makes forgery uneconomic.
